Ticket #18 — Support Ticket Assignment

Difficulty: Easy

Practice Metadata

  • Interview format: Engineering ticket / existing-code debugging.
  • Primary skills: priority ordering, FIFO behavior, load-aware dispatch.
  • Expected duration: 50–60 minutes.
  • AI assistance: Allowed in guided practice mode for explanations, hypotheses, test ideas, and focused hints; the candidate owns and explains every change.
  • Candidate objective: Trace why an older lower-priority ticket is selected and correct the dispatch order while preserving the assignment-load invariant.
  • Interviewer evaluation: Problem decomposition, code navigation, root-cause explanation, incremental implementation, and test evidence. See the shared interviewer rubric.

Context

You maintain dispatch for a support desk with billing and technical teams. Tickets have integer priorities from 1 (least urgent) to 5 (most urgent). FIFO means submission order is preserved among equally urgent tickets. Agent load is the count of tickets currently assigned to that agent.

Practice report

Create technical tickets low at priority 1, urgent at 5, and mid at 3 in that order. With all agent loads initially zero, call assign_next("technical").

Observation Current starter Expected
Ticket selected low urgent
Assigned agent Cal Cal

The next selection should be mid, assigned to the less-loaded eligible agent.

Core acceptance criteria

  • Select the highest-priority open ticket in the requested category. Equal priorities preserve submission order, and an assigned ticket is not dispatched again.
  • Assign the selected ticket to an eligible agent with the lowest current load. An empty category queue returns no ticket.
  • After assignment, the selected ticket has one assignee and that agent's load increases by one.

Optional follow-ups

If time remains, inspect malformed submissions, reassignment, and tie behavior for equally loaded agents. Agree on any unspecified tie policy with the interviewer before implementing it.

Out of Scope

Keep the configured teams and route response shapes. Agent availability, automatic escalation, ticket resolution, and changing the tie-breaking policy are outside this ticket.

Investigation

Reproduce the priority report and verify the selected ticket and agent load. Add a focused test for equal-priority FIFO ordering. Discuss how you would clarify an equal-load tie before choosing a policy.
